summary: iter-45 Round-10 hardening review. 13/14 tests PASS (7/7 TestRound10Hardening unit + 6/8 integration; 1 skipped is a dependent test). Poll-trades epoch fencing works flawlessly end-to-end (stale-epoch scalp trade cancelled + not leaked to EA; epoch>=max dispatches + raises max_order_epoch via $max; legacy no-epoch scalp dispatches; non-scalp trades unaffected). Service-block surfacing on GET /api/scalp/status audit works (null when indexes create OK). Suffixed-symbol tick regression passes. Full scalp suites still green: 114/114 in tests/unit/scalp + tests/integration/scalp. HOWEVER — the ledger-first P0-2 flow FAILS on the happy path because of a subtle race in scalp/engine.py `persist_risk_now` / `_fenced_account_write` fence checks: the check treats 'doc exists after our fence-missed update_one' as staleness, without comparing epochs — so when the async background `_persist_risk` upsert (kicked from `on_trade_closed`) inserts the risk doc BETWEEN our fence update_one and find_one, `apply_broker_deal` falsely returns 'applied: False' with error 'risk persist fenced out (stale lease epoch 1 < 1)'. Downstream: (a) scalp_financial_events doc stays status='pending' / risk_applied=False, (b) broker_deals stays financial_reconciliation_status='pending' with reconciliation_error set, EVEN THOUGH the background persist DID successfully write the same doc with applied_deal_ids and matching epoch. 100% reproducible with a single close deal on a fresh account owned by this worker. Crash-recovery test blocked / skipped (depends on the happy-path fix).

critical.issue: Fence-check false-positive: persist_risk_now (engine.py:983-990) and _fenced_account_write (engine.py:1009-1016) raise 'risk persist fenced out (stale lease epoch N < N)' when `existing is not None` — WITHOUT comparing the existing epoch against ours. The async background `_persist_risk` (kicked from `on_trade_closed` line 841) upserts the same doc with epoch=N between our update_one and find_one, causing find_one to return a doc that arrived via the SAME worker's own bg task, not via a newer owner. Because the raise is unconditional on existence, `apply_broker_deal` returns {applied: False}, the ledger event stays pending, `broker_deals` stays pending, and the whole ledger-first P0-2 fix silently fails on the happy path. Verified 100% reproducible with the ledger-first integration test.

action_items: FIX P0 race in scalp/engine.py::persist_risk_now — replace `if existing is not None: raise` with `if existing is not None and int(existing.get('lease_epoch') or 0) > epoch: raise` (equality means SAME owner won the insert race, not a newer owner).
SAME FIX in scalp/engine.py::_fenced_account_write for the `_ACCOUNT` doc branch (line 1013).

Alternative / defense-in-depth: consider dropping the fire-and-forget `_persist_risk` bg call from `on_trade_closed`/`on_partial_close` when the caller (`apply_broker_deal`) is going to await `persist_risk_now` immediately afterwards — the two writes race and duplicate the write anyway.
After the fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_iter45_round10_hardening.py — test_external_deal_creates_applied_ledger_event and test_crash_recovery_reconstructs_missing_ledger_event must both pass.
critical_code_review_comments: P0 · engine.py persist_risk_now (lines 978-990) and _fenced_account_write (lines 1004-1016): the fence-rejection path checks only `existing is not None`, not `existing.lease_epoch > epoch`. The `_bg`-scheduled `_persist_risk` from on_trade_closed inserts the doc between update_one and find_one → false-positive rejection → apply_broker_deal returns {applied: False} → ledger stays pending → broker_deals stays pending. The RCA is confirmed by inspecting scalp_risk_state after failure: applied_deal_ids contains the deal, lease_epoch matches — the bg persist DID succeed while the sync persist FALSELY reported stale.

P1 · scalp/engine.py apply_broker_deal (line 1322): the code calls persist_risk_now() after on_trade_closed() BUT on_trade_closed already fires a background _persist_risk. Two persistent writes to the same doc via two different code paths is inherently racy — the sync path should short-circuit the bg write, or the bg write should be conditionally suppressed when the sync one is guaranteed to run.

P2 · scalp/engine.py persist_risk_now:  `epoch = _lease_epoch.get(self.account_id, 0)` — when no lease has ever been acquired for this account (e.g. shortly after fresh apply_config restore), epoch defaults to 0 while a doc that was created via _bg could carry a higher epoch. Callers should ensure ensure_account_lease was called before persist_risk_now (apply_broker_deal does; scattered other callers should be audited).

P3 · bridge_routes.poll_trades (lines 562-573): the $max on scalp_owners.max_order_epoch happens BEFORE the read-back — so the fetch always sees the higher value and epoch < owner.max_order_epoch only fires when the incoming trade epoch is STRICTLY less than the highest epoch already observed. That's the intended semantic but easy to misread; a comment explaining the intentional read-after-write would help.

P4 · minor: bridge_routes.poll_trades doesn't return the epoch value in the response body, so a client-side EA cannot log the fencing decision — helpful for post-mortem forensics if a legitimate trade is ever cancelled.

P5 · scalp/engine.audit_backlog surfaces `service_block` but there is no API to CLEAR it once the offending unique-index was created out-of-band (seed.ensure_indexes only sets, never clears). A `set_service_block(None)` admin route would make ops recovery possible.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (P0 blocker for the Round-10 ledger-first fix): `persist_risk_now` and `_fenced_account_write` in scalp/engine.py have a two-step fence-check pattern: (1) `update_one({fence: {$or: [not_exists, $lte: epoch]}, ...})` and if matched_count==0, (2) `find_one(...)` and `if existing is not None: raise RuntimeError('stale lease epoch N < M')`. The rejection path assumes 'doc appeared → we're stale', BUT it never verifies the existing epoch is strictly greater than ours. The `_bg`-scheduled `_persist_risk` fired from `on_trade_closed` writes the SAME per-symbol scalp_risk_state doc (with our own worker's epoch) between our update_one and find_one, so find_one returns a doc with `lease_epoch == our epoch` — matching in theory, but the check only tests presence. Result: `apply_broker_deal` returns `{applied: False, reason: 'apply_failed: risk persist fenced out (stale lease epoch 1 < 1)'}` on the HAPPY PATH — the ledger event stays status='pending', risk_applied=False, broker_deals stays financial_reconciliation_status='pending' with reconciliation_error set. Ironically the P0-2 durability requirement is MET (bg _persist_risk DID persist applied_deal_ids + risk state) but the ledger-first state machine erroneously reports failure. REPRODUCTION: create an isolated TestBroker account (delete any existing scalp_owners doc so THIS worker acquires the lease), open a scalp_fast trade with matching mt5_ticket, POST /api/bridge/external-deal with deal_entry='out'. Every run produces the same error in backend.err.log. MITIGATION: in both fence-rejection branches, change `if existing is not None:` to `if existing is not None and int(existing.get('lease_epoch') or 0) > epoch:` — only truly-newer owners are stale. Optionally suppress the redundant bg _persist_risk when the sync path is imminent.
